memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, "Take handfuls of soot from a furnace and have Moses toss it into the air in the presence of Pharaoh. It will become fine dust over the whole land of Egypt, and festering boils will break out on people and animals throughout the land."" - Exodus 9:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This plague begins with soot from a furnace — very likely the kilns where Hebrew slaves baked bricks. The ash of Israel's suffering becomes the instrument of Egypt's judgement.

God does not forget where the pain came from. The furnace that consumed Hebrew lives now sends its ash across the land.

There is comfort in that for anyone who has been wronged. God keeps account. He does not need us to keep score, because He has never lost track. Paul says vengeance belongs to God, and that frees us to leave it with Him (Rom 12:19).

Notice the smallness of the action too. Moses throws a handful of soot into the air. That is all. A gesture no one would notice becomes a nationwide affliction.

God still works this way. Small obediences — a word spoken, a gift given, a prayer prayed — released into His hands can travel far beyond what we can see.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an injustice I need to hand over to God rather than carry?
2. What small act of obedience is God asking of me that seems insignificant?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I place my hurts in Your hands and trust Your justice. Use even my small obedience for Your purposes. Amen.
